# [STORY] As a security engineer, I want all hardcoded credentials and password disclosures removed from code, comments, and docs

## User Story
**As a** security engineer
**I want** all hardcoded passwords, default secret fallbacks, and credential disclosures removed from application configs, Dockerfiles, inline comments, Postman collections, and docs
**So that** the public repository adheres to secret management best practices and prevents accidental credential exposure

## Parent Epic
Parent: #76

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given `application.yml` files, `Dockerfile`s, and code comments, when they're audited, then no hardcoded password fallbacks (e.g. `admin123`, `redis123`, `postgres123`) remain in any of them
- [x] Given the Postman collection and documentation runbooks, when they reference credentials, then they use environment variable placeholders (e.g. `${MONGO_PASSWORD}`) instead of hardcoded secret strings
- [x] Given the local dev environment sources its config from `.env`, when `start-infrastructure.sh`/`docker-compose.yml` bring the stack up and `smoke-test.sh` runs against it, then both continue to pass 100%
- [x] Given the backend build, when it's run after the fallbacks are removed, then all unit/integration tests still pass
